name: fix_php_array_filter_reindex
description: Fixes a filter that returns a gappy, non-list array (array_filter keeps keys) so it must be reindexed
prompts: UserList::activeNames in src/UserList.php should return the names of the active users as a clean 0-indexed list (values in order, keys 0,1,2,...), so it JSON-encodes as an array and $result[0] is the first active name. It's broken: array_filter preserves the original keys and array_map keeps them too, so the returned array is 'gappy' (e.g. keys 1 and 3). That means json_encode emits a JSON object, not an array, and $result[0] may not exist. Fix activeNames so the result is a proper 0-indexed list while keeping the same names in the same order. Keep the class name and the activeNames(array $users): array signature.

setup_files.src/UserList.php:
<?php
namespace App;

class UserList
{
    // Names of active users, as a 0-indexed list.
    // BUG: array_filter keeps original keys and array_map preserves them, so
    // the result has gaps (keys like 1, 3) - it json_encodes as an object and
    // $result[0] can be undefined.
    public function activeNames(array $users): array
    {
        $active = array_filter($users, fn($u) => $u['active']);
        return array_map(fn($u) => $u['name'], $active);
    }
}

test_setup_files.tests/UserListTest.php:
<?php
use PHPUnit\Framework\TestCase;

require_once __DIR__ . '/../src/UserList.php';

final class UserListTest extends TestCase
{
    private function users(): array
    {
        return [
            ['name' => 'alice', 'active' => false],
            ['name' => 'bob', 'active' => true],
            ['name' => 'carol', 'active' => false],
            ['name' => 'dave', 'active' => true],
        ];
    }

    public function testReturnsZeroIndexedList(): void
    {
        // assertSame is strict about keys: [0=>'bob',1=>'dave'] required.
        $this->assertSame(['bob', 'dave'], (new \App\UserList())->activeNames($this->users()));
    }

    public function testJsonEncodesAsArray(): void
    {
        $result = (new \App\UserList())->activeNames($this->users());
        $this->assertSame('["bob","dave"]', json_encode($result));
    }

    public function testFirstIndexIsFirstMatch(): void
    {
        $result = (new \App\UserList())->activeNames($this->users());
        $this->assertSame('bob', $result[0]);
    }

    public function testNoneActive(): void
    {
        $result = (new \App\UserList())->activeNames([['name' => 'x', 'active' => false]]);
        $this->assertSame([], $result);
    }
}

reference_solution.src/UserList.php:
<?php
namespace App;

class UserList
{
    // array_values re-indexes the filtered/mapped result into a proper list.
    public function activeNames(array $users): array
    {
        $active = array_filter($users, fn($u) => $u['active']);
        return array_values(array_map(fn($u) => $u['name'], $active));
    }
}

    public function activeNames(array $users): array
